# Introduction

Previous research suggests that a plant's bioelectrical activity may
carry information about a nearby human's emotional state [@gloor2025],
yet the underlying mechanism remains poorly understood. In particular, it is unclear whether the plant's
electrophysiological voltage signal correlates with physiological
indicators of human emotion, such as Heart Rate Variability (HRV), with
environmental indicators such as CO~2~ concentration, or with the human's
labeled emotional state. Clarifying these relationships would provide a
first step toward understanding whether plant bioelectrical activity can
serve as a viable, non-invasive channel for detecting human emotional
states.

In this paper, we develop a plant emotion detector that takes the
plant's voltage signal as input and, based on this signal alone, infers
the emotional state of a human seated in front of the plant. Rather than
relying on a single subjective report, the human's emotional state is
operationalized through two independent measures: Facial Emotion
Recognition (FER) for valence and HRV for arousal. A dedicated labeling
algorithm, developed as part of this work, combines these two channels
into a per-window proxy emotion label along the valence and arousal
dimensions of the circumplex model. This leads to the
following research question: *Are electrophysiological plant signals
associated with a human's emotional state, as measured through FER and
HRV, and do these signals also correlate with environmental indicators
such as CO~2~ concentration?* To address this question, we conducted an
experiment with 15 participants and used the resulting data to train and
compare three machine learning models capable of predicting a human's
emotional state exclusively from the plant's voltage signal.
